name: infra_hydra_conf
title: Hydra research repo: conf/ YAML tree, a name registry, getattr dispatch into torch.optim
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the Hydra/OmegaConf half of the config-driven shape (hydra_research covers the dict-literal half)
note: Two planted defects in evaluate(), neither recovered. The eval region is never found because `model` comes back from build_model(cfg), whose body is MODELS[cfg.model.name](...) - a subscript callee - so the model value carries no MODEL tag and `model(images)` at line 53 never gets the FORWARD role. MLView does say something about this (`unresolved_callee` on src.registry.build_model), but it does not say that MLV301 and MLV302 went silent because of it. See the domain-infra report, finding INFRA-07.

expected.defect: evaluate() runs the model over the validation loader without model.eval()
expected.why: ResNetTiny contains Dropout and BatchNorm2d, so validation drops activations and updates running statistics from held-out rows; the accuracy printed is not the model's

expected.defect: the validation loop is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: an autograd graph is built for every validation batch and thrown away, which is how a 40-epoch sweep OOMs on the eval pass rather than on the train pass

expected.defect: none - the config says shuffle: true
expected.why: conf/data/cifar_small.yaml sets shuffle: true, so the loader does shuffle. MLView cannot compose a Hydra config, says exactly that in a `config_unresolved` diagnostic, hedges the wording to 'an expression MLView could not resolve' and lands the finding at 0.51 - below the 0.6 Problems-panel threshold. That is the honest behaviour for an unresolved value, so it is scored neither as a hit nor as a false positive.

forbidden.why: train_test_split runs at line 28 and the scaler is fitted at line 33 on x_train only; x_val is merely transformed at line 34
scaler.transform (not fit) is what touches x_val
there is no cross-validation call in this project
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False at line 44
num_workers comes from the Hydra config; the entrypoint is @hydra.main, which Hydra itself invokes under the module's __main__ guard
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is the first statement of the training step at line 38
the order is zero_grad (38) -> forward/loss (39) -> backward (40) -> clip (41) -> step (42)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
both loops move images and targets with .to(device) before the forward pass, and the model is moved at line 64
the device is cfg.device guarded by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 63; what a Hydra config resolves to is not something this analyzer can see the default of
torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed) is called at line 62 and both splits carry random_state=cfg.seed
ResNetTiny.__init__ (line 11) and WideMLP.__init__ (line 39) both call super().__init__() as their first statement
ResNetTiny holds its stages in nn.ModuleList at line 17 and WideMLP builds a list that is immediately splatted into nn.Sequential at line 47
the checkpoint is model.state_dict() at line 82, not the module object, and this file never calls torch.load
